BLOCKER: `runSwap` requires a full `Verify` (complete per-tenant checksums of `audit` vs `audit_partitioned`) to pass, but any audit write between prestage and swap lands only in the legacy table, so Verify fails hard; the designed "bounded delta drain under lock" is never reached and no quiesce/leadership step exists — the swap cannot complete on any live database.

`Swap` runs two full-table `count(*)` over the entire `audit` and shadow while holding ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, so freeze time scales with total table size rather than the delta, defeating the delta-bound and `audit_swap_freeze_seconds` budget contract.

`VerifyHoldExtraction` digests ALL archived hold rows (including released holds) against only currently-held live rows; after any hold is released the digests can never match, permanently blocking export/drop for that month.
MAJOR: The AC-required hold-reconcile path (hold placed AFTER archive → restore to scratch, extract, verify) has no implementation in Go or SQL; only the post-purge rejection exists.

The AC-required EDP service startup coverage check and ops cron emitting `audit_partition_months_ahead` / `audit_partition_low_coverage_total` plus stale-job alerting are absent — only the CLIs emit coverage.
`ExportMonth` writes the full plaintext month to a temp file on the ops host (0600 only); evidence-at-rest is required to be SSE-KMS — stream or encrypt before hitting disk.

`metrics.go` declares `MetricHoldAfterPurge`, `MetricInsertOutOfRange`, `MetricLateInsert`, `MetricProvisionSeconds`, `MetricHoldExtractFailed` that no code path ever emits, so the promised dashboards/alerts stay silent.
MINOR: Migration `0014` down drops the primitives but orphans helper functions (`audit_deny_truncate`, `audit_config_touch`, `audit_hold_guard`).
`RestoreMonth` leaves `audit_restore_YYYYMM` tables behind indefinitely (no TTL/drop) and they are invisible to `audit_assert_hardened`.
`pfaudit-retention purge --dry-run` prints a static message without consulting DB grace/hold state, so the dry-run plan is not the real plan.
Migration `0004` was edited in place (role-creation guard) instead of shipping a new migration — mutates applied migration history.
Metric name is `audit_swap_retry_exhausted_total` while the AC names `audit_swap_retry_exhausted`.
NIT: `RestoreMonth` doc comment says "scratch partition of the live audit table" but the code (correctly) creates a standalone table — comment drift.
`audit_restore_lock` is only a state-event insert, not a lock; the name misleads future maintainers.
The integration test attaches a partition via raw `CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF` + harden, bypassing `audit_attach_partition`, which the same diff declares the "only supported attach path".
`close` deletes the backup object without re-checking its existence/rehearsal at close time.
`rehearsal` asserts TOC presence via brittle substrings (`"TABLE public audit"`, `"SEQUENCE public audit_legacy_id_seq"`) that depend on `pg_restore -l` formatting.
SUMMARY: The migration substrate, privilege-enforced hardening and fail-closed out-of-range contract are genuinely strong and well-tested.
However the swap cannot succeed against a live writer workload (Verify gate + full-table counts under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE), and the hold-verification digest blocks retention after any released hold.
Two acceptance criteria — hold-reconcile and service/cron coverage telemetry with stale-job alerting — are unimplemented in this diff.
